bio: I study partial differential equations, with interests in fluid dynamics, regularity and ill-posedness, and aggregation–diffusion equations on curved spaces.

papers.title: Strong Ill-Posedness of the Surface Quasi-Geostrophic Equations in Wᵏ,¹(ℝ²)
papers.authors: Elaine Cozzi, Nicholas Harrison, and Zachary Radke
papers.description: We establish the ill-posedness of the surface quasi-geostrophic equations in Sobolev spaces W<sup>k,1</sup>(ℝ<sup>2</sup>) for every integer k ≥ 3. This includes the critical space W<sup>3,1</sup>(ℝ<sup>2</sup>). The proof is built on ideas developed in [BGZ26](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.04872), in particular the use of a theorem of Bonami and Poornima.

papers.title: Ill-Posedness of the 2D Euler Equations in a Logarithmically Refined Critical Sobolev Space
papers.authors: Elaine Cozzi, Nicholas Harrison, and Zachary Radke
papers.status: Journal of Dynamics and Differential Equations · 2026
papers.description: In [BL15](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-014-0548-6), Bourgain and Li establish strong ill-posedness of the 2D Euler equations for initial velocity in the critical Sobolev space H<sup>2</sup>(ℝ<sup>2</sup>). In this work, we extend the results of [BL15](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-014-0548-6) by demonstrating strong ill-posedness in logarithmically regularized spaces which are strictly contained in H<sup>2</sup>(ℝ<sup>2</sup>) and which contain H<sup>s</sup>(ℝ<sup>2</sup>) for all s > 2. These spaces are constructed via application of a fractional logarithmic derivative to the critical Sobolev norm. We show that if the power α of the logarithmic derivative satisfies α ≤ 1/2, then the 2D Euler equations are strongly ill-posed.

papers.title: Well-Posedness for the Euler Equations in Function Spaces of Generalized Smoothness
papers.description: We consider the question of well-posedness for the incompressible Euler equations in generalized function spaces of the type B<sup>s,ψ</sup><sub>p,q</sub>(ℝ<sup>d</sup>) and F<sup>s,ψ</sup><sub>p,q</sub>(ℝ<sup>d</sup>) where ψ is a slowly varying function in the Karamata sense and s = d/p + 1. We prove that if ψ grows fast enough, then there is a local in time solution to the Euler equations. We also establish a BKM-type criterion that allows us to obtain global existence in two dimensions.

papers.title: Local Existence for the 2D Euler Equations in a Critical Sobolev Space
papers.description: In the seminal work [5](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00222-014-0548-6), Bourgain and Li establish strong ill-posedness of the 2D incompressible Euler equations with vorticity in the critical Sobolev space W<sup>s,p</sup>(ℝ<sup>2</sup>) for sp = 2 and p ∈ (1, ∞). In this note, we establish short-time existence of solutions with vorticity in the critical space W<sup>2,1</sup>(ℝ<sup>2</sup>). Under the additional assumption that the initial vorticity is Dini continuous, we prove that the W<sup>2,1</sup>-regularity of vorticity persists for all time.
